gen-fs-styro-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big reads like a sturdy sans-serif with its terminals finishing well clear of the stem and its lowercase filling the line. Radio Canada Big would carry a long page without fuss, while Styro up top crowds its retro letters together.
gen-fs-styro-gf-readex-pro: Retro and tightly packed, Styro hits hard with its crowded little letters. And Readex Pro follows in a smooth, unvarying sans, so try the body a notch larger than feels necessary to use those broad terminal gaps.
gen-fs-styro-gf-roboto: Commanding Styro presses its letters shut, leaving barely any gap inside the e and c. Roboto does the opposite job, with generous mouths on its round letters, so Styro gets to be loud while Roboto keeps the reading easy.
gen-fs-styro-gf-ruda: Ruda reads like wire: a monoline skeleton, a sizable x-height, and wide-mouthed rounds that suit screens. Ruda against Styro's crowded retro heading is the whole appeal, a tightly packed display face above one with lots of room.
gen-fs-styro-gf-saira: Saira is a neutral sans-serif whose rounded letters stretch high and whose s lets you see right through it. Saira over a longer stretch stays open and legible, a sharp turn from Styro's closed, crowded heading above.
gen-fs-styro-gf-sarpanch:
Styro leads with a retro, commanding swagger.

Beneath it, Sarpanch opens up the lowercase e and keeps its x-height close to the ascenders, so the sans reads lighter against Styro's tightly closed, crowded letters.
gen-fs-styro-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Schibsted Grotesk brings big open e and a shapes with tall bowls, and its terminals never close in. Styro is the one to shout in retro fashion; Schibsted Grotesk quietly does the reading.
gen-fs-styro-gf-sen: Retro and crowded, Styro has a heavy, closed-up look with low stress in its curves. Sen then does the quieter work, tracing tall lowercase in a constant line while Styro handles the commanding part.
gen-fs-styro-gf-sintony: Clean is the first impression of Sintony, a chunky, tall-bodied sans with smooth curves. But Styro's retro, crowded heading gives it a sturdy partner, closed letters up top and open ones below.
gen-fs-styro-gf-sofia-sans: Styro packs its retro letters in until they nearly touch. Sofia Sans, with its tall acrylic-stencil lowercase and open-sided rounds, can take a slightly generous size to show off that clarity.
